semantic_rules: descriptor address is exactly IPv4 127.0.0.1 or IPv6 ::1 and port is nonzero
descriptor is signed by the Device named inside it and has a positive lifetime of at most 86400 seconds
request names the exact signed descriptor and repeats its nonzero 32-byte bearer token
request has a nonzero caller-generated correlation ID and a positive lifetime of at most 30 seconds
request validity is contained by descriptor validity and both are current within the bounded clock-skew policy
wait-for-change timeout is between 1 and 120000 milliseconds
response is signed by the exact Device named by the descriptor
response binds the descriptor ID, request ID and digest of the complete canonical request
pong repeats the descriptor Account and Device identities
change-state is valid only for wait-for-change; changed true requires a greater revision and changed false requires the exact requested revision
shutdown-accepted is valid only for shutdown while a bounded nonempty UTF-8 error is valid for every command
conversation-list reads are explicitly paginated by the deterministic label and peer Account tuple with at most 64 summaries per response
conversation summaries are strictly ordered and bind their label-derived Conversation ID, exact endpoint counts, one primary endpoint, endpoint health and latest-message preview
history reads bind the label-derived Conversation ID, a nonzero immutable snapshot ID, at most 100 messages and at most 196608 aggregate plaintext body bytes
history continuation arithmetic is exact: the next before-index plus returned message count equals the requested page end
every read response is signed by the descriptor Device and commits to the digest of the complete read request
contact enrollment binds the exact peer Account, descriptor path and label-derived conversation identity to a domain-separated canonical contact ID
a successful contact result repeats the exact peer Account and derives its contact ID from the local Account, peer Account and label-derived Conversation ID
own-device-directory status repeats the exact descriptor Account and Device and bounds the active roster to at most 32 Devices
device-directory receipt identity and generation are coupled while convergence and restart-recovery states are consistent with the applied and launch profile paths
apply-own-device-directory embeds the exact Root-signed candidate list and anchors the expected current authority revision and domain-separated signed-list digest
the current and candidate lists name the descriptor Account while the running descriptor Device remains present with a byte-identical certificate
a candidate is either an exact idempotent replay or a newer Root-signed authority state retaining every previously observed revocation
live application cannot add or replace a Device certificate; every removed Device must have a permanent Root revocation in the candidate authority snapshot
the signed mutation result binds the exact previous and resulting revisions and digests, exact removed Device set and resulting directory status
an idempotent equal-revision result reports no newly retired ratchet or prekey records and no newly published ticket
future recipient exclusion does not claim remote rewriting or erasure: preexisting ciphertext is immutable and existing history copies remain readable
queue-message carries one nonempty UTF-8 body of at most 65536 bytes and names a peer Account distinct from the descriptor Account
the caller-generated nonzero request ID is also the durable queue ID; retrying the exact request is idempotent while reuse for different content must fail closed
a successful queue result repeats the exact peer Account and derives Conversation and canonical contact IDs from the requested label and Accounts
the inserted flag reports only whether the exact durable queue record was newly created; false is valid only for an already-present byte-equivalent record
the active adapter must verify enrolled contact and current conversation membership under the same state lock as durable queue insertion
outbox-status-page has a limit from 1 through 128 and either starts a new projection or supplies a nonzero content-derived snapshot ID with an exact start index
an outbox snapshot ID is the domain-separated digest of the complete globally counted projection sorted by strictly increasing Queue ID
outbox global counters exactly equal the complete snapshot item states and bound contacts, queue items and retry records
every non-delivered item is pending, every non-queued item is materialized and only delivered items carry one nonzero acknowledgement Event ID
each signed outbox page repeats the immutable snapshot ID and global counters, contains at most the requested bounded limit and preserves strict Queue ID order
outbox continuation arithmetic is exact: the next start index equals the requested start plus returned items and retains the same snapshot ID until the queue count is reached
the active adapter must retain the exact snapshot for continuation or fail explicitly as stale after state drift or restart; it must never rebuild changed contents under an existing cursor
provider import embeds one canonical signed storage offer and independently enforces its signature, current validity and bounded admission work before registry mutation

provider results carry the original signed offer plus only a nonzero transport identity and bounded observation time; duplicated unauthenticated endpoint, store, policy or capacity strings are forbidden
provider import results repeat the exact requested offer, report inserted, replaced or already-present and bound the active registry count to at most 4096
provider selection uses a nonzero opaque salt, requests between one and eight entries and repeats the exact salt and requested count in the signed result
a selected provider set contains at most the requested and active counts, has unique store keys and offer IDs and exposes no mailbox read or write capability
the active adapter must execute selection against one current read-only registry snapshot under the existing bootstrap-safe corroboration and path-diversity policy
mailbox-capability-status-page has a limit from 1 through 16 and either starts a new projection or supplies a nonzero content-derived snapshot ID with an exact start index
each mailbox capability head embeds one independently verified Device-signed canonical update and at most one matching recipient-signed acknowledgement
a capability status snapshot contains at most 1024 strictly ordered unique chain heads and commits the descriptor Account and Device, exact aggregate counts and all heads
every projected head names the descriptor Account and Device as exact owner or exact recipient; unrelated capability chains fail closed
page heads cannot exceed any signed aggregate bucket, while a complete one-page response must exactly reproduce all counters and the content-derived snapshot ID
mailbox capability status contains no local binding, read secret, write secret or decrypted peer offer; the signed update may retain only its recipient-sealed peer offer
mailbox capability creation embeds an exact Device-signed provider selection containing two through eight strictly store-key-ordered current volunteer offers with distinct transport identities
mailbox capability rotation and revocation embed the exact currently acknowledged active predecessor head; the active adapter must compare it atomically with the local chain head before commit
mailbox capability create starts generation one without a predecessor, while rotate and revoke advance exactly one generation and satisfy the signed canonical update-chain link

create and rotate produce exact-volunteer activation updates whose replica set exactly equals the embedded provider selection and whose bounded offer expiry does not exceed any selected provider offer
revoke preserves the active binding identifier, carries no provider selection or offer expiry and produces only a recipient-acknowledgement-pending signed revocation update
the mutation request ID is the durable idempotency key: exact retry may return already-committed while reuse for different bytes must fail before state mutation
mailbox mutation responses contain no local binding, read secret, write secret or decrypted peer offer and bind the complete request digest under the descriptor Device signature

the active adapter must exact-compare the recipient authority digest, current provider registry selection and predecessor head under one state lock before creating local secrets or committing an update
publication-channel rotation embeds the exact expected current public capability, channel epoch, peer scope digest and latest accepted publication head
the next publication channel epoch advances exactly once and the successor capability must differ from the exact current capability

the successor publication capability is never caller supplied: the active runtime re-derives the exact current capability and derives its successor internally from its local Device secret, exact durable peer scope and respective epochs
the publication rotation response exposes only public capability material and contains neither the local Device secret nor the plaintext durable peer scope
the rotation ID commits the complete request digest, successor public capability and next channel epoch
a successful local rotation remains awaiting first network publication and pending peer delivery, requires no runtime restart and performs no network operation
the publication rotation request ID is the durable idempotency key: one state lock exact-compares and commits the transition while an exact retry may return already-committed
publish-own-ticket commits the exact current public channel head plus a nonzero recipient Device-list digest and a recipient count from one through 32
the runtime creates the signed ticket and HPKE envelope internally; ticket plaintext, HPKE ciphertext, write secrets and local paths never cross the canonical IPC boundary
a publish result advances the accepted publication generation exactly once without changing contact, peer, scope, channel epoch or public capability
the returned canonical write authorization exactly binds the updated public capability, new generation, opaque envelope byte length and raw BLAKE3 envelope digest
publish success requires a canonical root-only HTTPS service origin and reports confirmed HTTP success but remains pending a separate peer Device observation
refresh-contact-ticket commits the exact contact, peer publisher Device, channel and local observation and publication high-water heads
the runtime fetches, authenticates and decrypts the opaque envelope internally and atomically installs the ticket before returning success
a refresh result carries an independently verifiable local Device-signed observation that advances the observation generation exactly once and strictly advances publication generation
HTTPS success is only a Device-signed report of the completed exchange and is not independent proof of remote durability or later peer delivery
the publication-network request ID is the durable idempotency key: one state lock exact-compares network and local effects while an exact retry may return the byte-identical already-committed result

the sensitive portable Device request, Root response, publication write keys and replacement-ticket plaintext remain inside a trusted content-addressed staging area and never cross this local IPC boundary

the request-created result exposes only a compact public request claim, proof identity, requester Device, bounded artifact references and an awaiting-offline-Root state
apply-publication-conflict-response requires the exact pending public request claim and names only the bounded digest and length of a separately staged Root response
the runtime independently verifies the staged Root signature against the exact current Account authority and requires the response claim to match every public field of the pending request ceremony
apply success requires one atomic commit that replaces the peer endpoint ticket, retains the Root resolution, releases the matching quarantine and preserves the original conflict proof
a locally applied Root resolution remains pending propagation to exact-current sibling Devices and does not claim remote convergence
publication-conflict artifact references use a dedicated domain-separated digest; filesystem paths, Root secrets, write capabilities and artifact plaintext are forbidden
the publication-conflict IPC request ID is the durable idempotency key: an exact retry may return the byte-identical already-committed result while divergent reuse fails before staging or mutation

configuration names one active sibling Device distinct from the descriptor Device and references its current connection ticket only by a bounded byte length and domain-separated content digest
a policy starts at generation one without a predecessor and every replacement advances exactly one generation from the exact expected policy ID
the policy ID commits the Account, local Device, authority state, policy generation, predecessor, configuration time and complete bounded configuration
announcement intervals, ticket validity, retry bounds and the four-bit Ethernet, Wi-Fi, mobile and unknown network mask are explicit and fail closed outside their limits
scheduler state is derived from enabled state, current network permission and failure count rather than accepted as an independent runtime claim
attempt, success, next-attempt, bundle and transport option tuples are internally consistent, nonzero when present and temporally ordered
status contains at most 32 unique policies in strict recipient Device order and its snapshot ID commits the complete authority-bound current-network projection
configuration and status results require no restart, execute only while the foreground runtime is running and explicitly deny an OS background service
filesystem paths, recipient ticket plaintext, Account Root secrets and publication write capabilities are forbidden from this own-device announcement IPC surface
the configure request ID is the durable idempotency key: an exact retry may return already-committed while stale predecessor or divergent reuse fails before policy mutation
own-device ticket discovery commands embed the exact current Root-signed Account Device list and bind every response to its authority revision and domain-separated signed-list digest

discovery configuration names one active sibling distinct from the descriptor Device, uses a canonical root-only HTTPS origin and bounds publication TTL, refresh lead, announcement timing, retry and network mask
the runtime derives both directional pairwise capabilities internally; IPC exposes only distinct nonzero channel identifiers and never exposes a reusable read or write capability
a discovery policy starts at generation one without a predecessor, advances from the exact expected policy and commits both channel identifiers with the complete authority-bound configuration
an installed locator binds a nonzero publication generation, ordered publication and expiry times, one bounded content-addressed ticket artifact and one nonzero authenticated observation identifier
the installed locator and child announcement policy identifier are atomically absent or present so a fetched ticket cannot be reported without its announcement handoff

workflow state is derived from enabled state, network permission, failures, outbound publication, inbound locator and announcement success as disabled, blocked, awaiting publish, awaiting fetch, awaiting announcement, backoff or synchronized
attempt, success, next-attempt, bundle and transport option tuples are internally consistent, nonzero when present and temporally ordered; success also requires an installed locator
discovery status contains at most 32 unique policies in strict recipient Device order and its snapshot ID commits the complete authority-bound current-network projection

ticket plaintext, HPKE envelope bytes, Device encryption secrets, derived capabilities, local paths and Account Root secrets are forbidden; request ID is the durable idempotency key and stale predecessor or divergent reuse fails before mutation

the child projection contains exactly every active sibling Device and every retained nonlocal permanent revocation from the supplied Root-signed roster
roster children are unique, limited to 64 and ordered strictly by recipient Device ID; omission, duplication, reordering or an unknown child fails closed
each active child deterministically inherits the parent configuration while each retired tombstone is forced disabled and both inherit the parent's configured timestamp
every child policy ID is recomputed from the exact authority state, derived configuration, generation, predecessor and directional public channel identifiers
the roster snapshot ID atomically commits the Account, local Device, authority state, current network, parent policy and complete ordered child projection
declared active and retired counts exactly match the child projection and the runtime serializes reconciliation with exactly one maximum parallel workflow
roster configuration and status require no restart, execute only while the foreground runtime is running and explicitly deny an OS background service
Account Root secrets, Device signing or encryption secrets, derived read or write capabilities, ticket plaintext, HPKE ciphertext and local filesystem paths are forbidden from roster IPC
an exact retry may return already-committed only for the unchanged parent head and projection; stale predecessor, divergent reuse or a mismatched roster fails before mutation
recovery-plan approval embeds one independently verified source-Device-signed recovery link and the exact full SAS digest explicitly confirmed by the local user
the approved recovery link names the descriptor Account and exact descriptor Device as recipient; cross-Account, cross-Device and self-substituted context fails closed
plan approval occurs inside the signed link validity interval and chooses a validity from 3600 through 604800 seconds without arithmetic overflow
the descriptor Device signs the exact link, SAS, explicit Ethernet, Wi-Fi, mobile, unknown-network and external-power policy, approval time and expiry as one canonical recovery plan
the recovery-plan record ID commits the complete signed plan and the optional immutable cancellation tombstone
status addresses one nonzero plan ID and returns only custody state bound to the exact descriptor Account and recipient Device
cancellation exact-compares both the plan ID and current content-addressed record ID so stale or concurrent state cannot be silently overwritten
cancellation creates one descriptor-Device-signed user-requested tombstone whose time is not earlier than plan approval and preserves the original signed plan
approved lifecycle requires no cancellation while cancelled lifecycle requires one matching valid tombstone; every inconsistent combination fails closed
approval, status and cancellation report restart-not-required, foreground-runtime-only execution and an explicitly disabled OS background service
the execution policy permits at least one network class and remains custody metadata only until a separately specified recovery executor consumes it
recovery-plan custody performs no history transfer, network connection, remote deletion or convergence claim and carries no recovery page payload
Account Root secrets, Device private keys, private recovery capabilities, decrypted history and local filesystem paths are forbidden from this recovery-plan IPC surface
the request ID is the durable idempotency key: exact replay may return already-committed while stale record IDs or divergent reuse fail before plan or tombstone mutation
unknown variants, noncanonical CBOR, trailing data, expired objects and contextual substitutions fail closed
recovery execution starts only from an approved current plan and exact content-addressed plan record named by the request
the approved plan Account and recipient Device exactly match the current signed descriptor before scheduler state is created
routine IPC may start or inspect recovery but cannot supply network observations, power observations, attempt outcomes, checkpoints or scheduler transitions
the recipient Device signs every scheduler state and each noninitial state commits the exact predecessor state identifier and increments generation once
scheduler initialization creates a recipient-signed canonical checkpoint at the approved range start and binds the complete plan identity

attempt-failed transitions preserve the checkpoint, increment consecutive failure count and bind one nonzero failure code
retry delay uses deterministic equal jitter bound to plan ID, failure exponent and attempt ordinal and is capped by the signed retry policy
attempt-progressed and completed transitions require a valid signed successor checkpoint for the exact plan and reset consecutive failures
completion requires the checkpoint cursor to equal the approved range end while partial progress must remain strictly before it
plan cancellation produces only a terminal cancellation transition and cannot revive or overwrite a completed scheduler chain
scheduler time never moves backward; a backward observation is reported explicitly and an expired attempt lease cannot be presented as active
readiness is derived from signed lifecycle, plan expiry, retry deadline, exact network class and external-power policy rather than caller assertion
execution snapshots embed the exact verified plan state and signed scheduler head and bind their derived readiness to the observation context
execution status and start responses require no restart, execute only in the foreground runtime and explicitly deny an OS background service
Account Root secrets, Device private keys, private recovery capabilities, decrypted history, page payloads and local filesystem paths are forbidden from recovery execution IPC
the request ID is the durable execution idempotency key: exact replay may return already committed while divergent reuse or a stale plan record fails before scheduling
the execution contract makes no claim that a source is online, that a page was transferred, that history converged or that any remote copy was erased
the active Postcard adapter uses explicit IPC version 27 with descriptor signature domain v8 and rejects version 26 descriptors and requests before actor dispatch

the completion inventory contains every canonical command/result pair and its owning module, and its command and result sequences exactly match this schema
